transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Anika Sharma (CTO, BrightWave), Jordan Lee (ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (Head infra), Priya Desai (Security)

Summary:
Quick sign-off on go/no-go gates, agree exact numerical thresholds, finalize benchmark reporting CSV/JSON format, align on load profile (concurrency / burst), and confirm timeline for the first 1-hour run. Also clarifying security/compliance delivery expectations.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria: latency percentiles, accuracy/QA thresholds, cost-per-1000-token targets, error rate ceilings
- Workload sizing: average tokens per request, peak concurrency, expected sustained RPS
- Benchmarks: synthetic vs replay, golden eval set, dataset labeling expectations
- Reporting: required fields for results.csv / results.json, anonymization, and attachment of raw traces
- Timeline and responsibilities

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick agenda. goal is to lock the quantitative gates for the pilot and confirm reporting format. If we can get these thresholds live today, we can run the first benchmark next week.
[00:18] Anika Sharma: Sounds good. We wanna make sure it's realistic for production traffic not just toy queries. so anything you propose has to map to our EHR redaction flow and clinical question answering.
[00:28] Luis Ortega: Totally. we've already looked at the sample prompts you sent, Jordan, and we're building a synthetic replay that keeps token distributions and response lengths intact. quick note — some names in the samples got munged in our import, so please double-check the gold labels you'll share.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: Yeah I saw that, there was some OCR hiccup on older PDFs. I'll resubmit a cleaned set.
[00:52] Tom Reynolds: For sizing, peak concurrency for our front end is about 120 concurrent reqs, sustained around 45. bursts up to 200 for short periods. that's our real constraint.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Great — let's map that to two benchmark phases: Phase A (latency-focused, small batch) and Phase B (throughput, sustained load). We recommend p50/p95/p99 samples plus tail error rate.
[01:29] Priya Desai: Also we need to confirm that logs sent to Redwood (if any) will be PII-stripped. we can't ship raw PHI out of our VPC.
[01:42] Luis Ortega: Understood — for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed VPC and optional KMS. For hosted we can enable token redaction and prefix-only caching; we'll include artifact notes in the security pack.
[01:58] Anika Sharma: Okay. now the gates: from our side, the product team wants accuracy high given regulatory context. can you suggest concrete numbers?
[02:10] Luis Ortega: Based on initial evals on the sample set, our baseline with the r-instruct-7b-ish variant showed 89% exact-match on your label schema. For acceptable pilot we'd propose: accuracy >= 92% on canonical eval set, p95 latency < 350ms for single streaming token latency for hosted, and error rate (5xx/timeout) < 0.5% across the run. Cost target — staying under $3.50 per 1k tokens for the baseline workload. Those are ballpark; want to see if BrightWave can accept.
[02:47] Anika Sharma: 92% is a high bar but reasonable for the use cases we care about. about latency — for clinical UI we prefer sub-300ms p95 but we recognise that with privacy-preserving and longer context that's tricky. any options to trade off?
[03:05] Luis Ortega: Yes — we can propose two parallel gates: strict gate for interactive workflows (p95 < 300ms) and a relaxed gate for batch/long-context flows (p95 < 500ms) — the pilot should mark the interactive subset. If interactive fails but batch passes, that's a partial pass and we mark mitigation steps.
[03:26] Maya Chen: I want to be explicit about pass/fail rules. propose go/no-go rules:
- Full Pass: interactive gate and accuracy gate both met, error rate under threshold, and cost target within 10%
- Conditional Pass: accuracy gate met but interactive latency missed by <=15% and documented mitigation (quantization or VPU) accepted
- Fail: accuracy < 90% or error rate > 1% or cost > 30% above target
[04:00] Jordan Lee: That seems fair. For the accuracy metric we need clarity: are we doing exact match, fuzzy F1, or human-in-the-loop acceptability?
[04:12] Luis Ortega: We'll compute both exact-match and a weighted F1; the official gate will be exact-match >= 92%, and we'll include F1 as supporting evidence. Human review will be a spot check for edge cases — 50 random examples.
[04:28] Anika Sharma: Okay. And reporting — what will you deliver after a run? we need CSV/JSON that we can ingest into our dashboard.
[04:37] Luis Ortega: Deliverables per run: results.csv with columns: request_id, prompt_hash (anonymized), ground_truth_label, model_output, exact_match (0/1), f1_score, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_code; plus a results.json that includes aggregated metrics — p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput RPS, error_rate, cost_estimate, and raw trace links (if permitted). We'll also attach the load profile file and the run command used.
[05:06] Priya Desai: Make sure prompt_hash is irreversible and no PHI — use salted sha256 on canonicalized prompt. we will provide the salt to you for verification, not the raw.
[05:18] Luis Ortega: Absolutely. we'll include hashing step in the harness.
[05:22] Tom Reynolds: For the throughput run, what's the recommended warmup? We don't want cold-start dominating numbers.
[05:30] Luis Ortega: Standard is 10 minutes warmup at 30% load, then ramp to target over 5 minutes, sustain for the target hour, then cool down. We'll include agent-level KV cache priming where appropriate.
[05:43] Maya Chen: On the topic of models and quantization: we propose testing two model variants during pilot — one FP16 high-accuracy and one int8 quantized lower-cost variant. acceptance should note which model met gates.
[05:57] Anika Sharma: We also want to exercise fallback behavior — if the primary model breaches latency during burst, the system should auto-route to the cost-optimized variant. that behavior should be observable in the report.
[06:12] Luis Ortega: We'll instrument routing events and include route-switch timestamps in trace logs.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: For the eval set size — we suggested 500 canonical examples earlier. is that sufficient for statistical significance?
[06:27] Luis Ortega: 500 is a pragmatic start; we'll compute confidence intervals. if you want tighter bounds, we recommend 1,000+. for this pilot 500 gives a quick read and lets us iterate.
[06:38] Anika Sharma: Fine for now. timeline-wise what's realistic?
[06:43] Maya Chen: Plan: 11/19 - Redwood sends harness; 11/20 - BrightWave sends canonical eval + salt; 11/22 - Redwood runs Phase A (latency) locally with your dataset in replay mode and shares initial report; 11/29 - full throughput 1-hour run; 12/2 - joint review and signoff meeting.
[07:05] Tom Reynolds: We need the run to happen in our VPC or dedicated lane. will Redwood be able to orchestrate the Dedicated instance in our AWS account?
[07:15] Luis Ortega: Yes we support Dedicated in customer account; we'll need IAM role and some networking bits. we'll share infra checklist as part of the harness repo.
[07:25] Priya Desai: And for compliance, send the SOC2 summary and encryption-at-rest docs. we'll need KMS integration notes.
[07:33] Maya Chen: I'll attach our security pack and the KMS integration guide.
[07:38] Anika Sharma: One more item — reporting cadence and who signs off on pass vs fail. BrightWave will appoint a product owner (Anika) and an ML stake (Jordan) to co-sign. Redwood will present an official results packet, and signoff will be a joint decision.
[07:54] Maya Chen: Noted. we'll include a short signoff form in the report.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: A question — what's the plan for regression guarding? we don't want later model swaps to silently degrade quality.
[08:06] Luis Ortega: We'll provide eval automation that can be re-run per release; and Redwood Optimize can run nightly sample checks and trigger an alert if exact-match drops > 3% on the canonical set. we'll show how to wire that to your webhook or Slack.
[08:20] Anika Sharma: Good. ok that's enough high level. can we summarize the numeric gates we agreed on?
[08:27] Maya Chen: Yes: accuracy (exact-match) >= 92% on canonical 500-ex example set; interactive p95 latency < 300ms (alternate relaxed p95 < 500ms for long-context); error rate < 0.5% (fail if > 1%); cost target < $3.50 per 1k tokens (fail if > $4.55).
[08:50] Tom Reynolds: We'll accept conditional pass if interactive latency missed by <=15% but with mitigation.
[08:56] Luis Ortega: For reporting format — results.csv + results.json as outlined. We'll provide example templates in the harness repo.
[09:04] Priya Desai: security note: any logs we permit must be hashed and stored in a customer-controlled bucket.
[09:10] Luis Ortega: We'll include an option to write artifacts to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[09:15] Maya Chen: Great. next steps recap — we covered those in the action items. anything else?
[09:22] Anika Sharma: One last ask: can Redwood provide an estimate of expected token cost for our example 45 reqs/min sustained load? we want a rough monthly projection.
[09:33] Luis Ortega: Sure. rough calc on current numbers: average prompt tokens 450, response 200 => ~650 tokens per request. at 45 RPS sustained (~2,700/min) that's ~1.76M tokens/hour. multiply for daily/monthly we can send a spreadsheet.
[09:52] Maya Chen: We'll attach a cost projection sheet with sensitivity ranges.
[09:56] Jordan Lee: thanks all. look forward to the harness.
[10:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the repo and schedule the first run window.

Meeting end.

Notes on artifacts shared in call:
- Redwood: benchmark harness repo link (to be shared), results.csv template, results.json schema, security pack (SOC2 summary + KMS notes)
- BrightWave: cleaned canonical eval set (500 examples), salt for hashing, VPC/IAM contact info

References / links mentioned:
- sample run command: ./run_benchmark --profile brightwave-interactive --warmup 600 --sustain 3600
- results.csv template columns: request_id,prompt_hash,ground_truth,model_output,exact_match,f1,latency_ms,tokens_in,tokens_out,error_code
- results.json keys: aggregated_metrics,latency_percentiles,throughput,errors,cost_estimate,model_variant

End of transcript.
